newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen unable to meet U.S. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen unable to meet U.S. envoy.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen will not be able to meet a visiting U.S. envoy this weekend due to the poor health of the prime minister's mother, an aide to Hun Sen said on Friday.
Hun Sen has been attending his seriously ill mother at a Phnom Penh hospital in recent days.
"He has cancelled all his meetings for the next few days because of his mother's sickness," said Prak Sokhonn, an adviser to Hun Sen.
U.S. special envoy Desaix Anderson was due to arrive in Phnom Penh on Saturday and hoped to meet Hun Sen for talks, an official at the U.S. embassy said earlier.
Hun Sen ousted his former coalition partner and co-prime minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in a bloody July 6 takeover.
The United States suspended its aid programme to Cambodia for 30 days in response to the coup.

A U.S. government official said Wednesday's vote in the Cambodian parliament approving Foreign Minister Ung Huot's nomination as first prime minister in place of Ranariddh was undemocratic due to the atmosphere of intimidation in the country.
Ung Huot was formally appointed first prime minister on Thursday and an official in Washington said the U.S. would deal with him.

Anderson did not have a meeting with Ung Huot planned, the U.S. embassy official said. Anderson was meeting representatives of non governmental organisations in Cambodia before his departure on Sunday, the official said.
